comments.author: @johnferrellesq.
comments.text: It's encouraging that we are seeing more software inventors having success in the patent office in recent years.  One thing I forgot to mention in this video, however, is that it's still important to focus on observable inventions.  If the invention is buried deep in the code and can't be observed, it's probably not worth wasting a patent to protect it.  Good luck with your projects!  -john

comments.author: @GuanglinDu
comments.text:
5:06 How to optimally and efficiently file patent applications and write patent claims related to software patents?
(1) Think of a general purpose computer as being specialized or defined by the software steps that are programming the hardware.
(2) Emphasize the value and advantage of executing the process on a computer. That is the software program does things using a computer that only a computer can do, e.g., a malware detector.
(3) Find a feedback loop in your software program that is where a data set or a prior result is used in creating a new result. That new result is used to update the data set and used in the next calculation. The calculations continually improve because of this feedback loop. This really is the basis of learning systems and AI systems. I found these elements to be highly patentable.
(4) It's still important to focus on observable inventions.  If the invention is buried deep in the code and can't be observed, it's probably not worth wasting a patent to protect it.
